newsitem.title: USA: OLYMPICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON NAMED USOC SPORTSMAN OF THE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON NAMED USOC SPORTSMAN OF THE YEAR.

text.p: Track superstar Michael Johnson, who pulled off an unprecedented Olympic golden double at the Atlanta Games, on Wednesday was named the 1996 SportsMan of the Year by the United States Olympic Committee.

Johnson, who became the first man ever to win the 200 and 400 meters races at the same Olympics, received 80 of 104 first-place votes in USOC balloting to earn SportsMan of the Year honours for the third time in four years.

Speedskater Eric Heiden (1977, 1979, 1980) is the only other three-time winner of the USOC award, given annually since its inception in 1974. The 29-year-old Johnson previously won the honour in 1993 and 1995.

On July 29, Johnson won the 400 meters in an Olympic record time of 43.49 seconds. Three days later, he clocked an astonishing world record time of 19.32 in the 200 meters, shattering his own record by three-tenths of a second.
Swimmer Jeff Rouse, a double gold medal winner, was second in the voting, followed by volleyball star Karch Kiraly.
Swimmer Amy Van Dyken, who won four gold medals in the Olympics this summer, Tuesday was named the 1996 SportsWoman of the Year.
